In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanism by which SopA, a protein of the F plamid, polymerizes to form a filament that is involved in the partitioning of the plasmid to the daughter cells during cell division of Escherichiacoli.
the mechanism of the active equi-parition of the F plsmid and the regulation of the F plasmd partitioning.
the regulation of the SopABC protein complex, which mediates the equi-partitioning of the Escherichia F plasmid, and the mechanism of polymerization of Sopa, a component of the complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SopA polymerizes to form a network, which is stabilized by SopB and inhibited by DNA.
SopB and SopA are involved in active equi-partitioning of F plasmid by binding to the sopAB and sopC promoters, respectively, and by stimulating the polymerization and disassembly of SopA.
SopB is required for SopA polymer formation and SopA-SobB interactions are required for SopB to stimulate SopA polymer disassembly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sopABC genes have evolved to achieve an active equi-partitioning of the plasmid, and SopA-SobB interactions are important for this.
SopB accelerates disassembly (and possibly also assembly) of SopA and that SopA-SBopB interactions are mediated through SopB domains.
SopA and SopB are both required for active equi-partioning and that SopB is a new factor for SopA polymer assembly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SopB and SopA have new roles in polymerization of the SopABC system.
the F plasmids use DNA and Sop proteins to achieve active equi-parition of the plasmid.
SopB protein is not only a DNA-binding protein, but also an active component of SopA assembly.
